newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Guatemala hosting meeting on murdered journalists.
newsitem.headline: Guatemala hosting meeting on murdered journalists.

text.p: The Interamerican Press Association (IAPA) announced on Friday it will hold a conference here in July to draw attention to murders of journalists throughout the Americas.

"The conference is to analyse the issue, to make recommendations and protests and to call public and government attention to the issue," Uruguayan journalist Danilo Arbilla, president of IAPA's Press Freedom Commission, told reporters at a news conference on Friday.
Arbilla said 169 journalists were killed in the Americas in the past seven years and almost none of the cases have been solved.
For two years the commission has studied six sample cases of killings of journalists, two each from Guatemala, Mexico and Colombia.

"We are shown in these six cases a very sad story. In almost all of the cases the governments have done almost nothing. It is a shame. It is a crime and the situation must change," David Lawrence, editor of the Miami Herald and ex-president of IAPA said.
The commission will present the final report from the study, "Unpunished Crimes against Journalists", at the conference.
IAPA has invited human rights and legal experts from throughout the Americas as well as supreme court justices from Mexico, Guatemala and Colombia, to the conference.

The six cases IAPA has studied closely are Colombians Guillermo Cano Isaza and Carlos Lajud Catalan, Guatemalans Jorge Carpio Nicolle and Irma Flaquer Azurdia, and Mexicans Hector Felix Miranda and Victor Manuel Oropeza.
